summary: The Satellite and Telecommunications Streamlining Act (SAT Streamlining Act) establishes strict deadlines and procedures for the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to review and process satellite licenses, earth station authorizations, and market access petitions. It requires the FCC to make completeness determinations on applications within 30 days and generally grant or deny completed applications within one year. It also prevents state and local governments from regulating the rates of these licensees.

affected_groups.effect: They face mandatory deadlines for FCC license processing, potential 'deemed granted' approvals if deadlines are missed, and streamlined rules for minor modifications and replacements.
They are included in the new mandatory FCC processing deadlines and notification-only provisions for adding certain authorized space stations.
They are prohibited from regulating the rates charged by satellite licensees or market access grantees.
The agency must issue new implementation rules, adhere to strict application review timelines, establish interagency coordination with the Department of Commerce, and submit annual backlog reports.

key_provisions: Requires the FCC to review and make completeness determinations on license and market access applications within 30 days.
Sets a one-year deadline for the FCC to grant or deny completed applications for space station licenses, earth stations, and market access.
Provides a 'deemed granted' mechanism if the FCC fails to meet application or renewal deadlines after receiving written notice from the applicant.
Establishes expedited 30-day and 90-day review tracks for certain license modifications, such as technical replacements and capacity improvements.
Mandates formal reviews for national security and law enforcement concerns by referring applicants with reportable foreign ownership to an interagency committee.
Prohibits state and local governments from regulating the rates charged by licensees or market access grantees.
Directs the FCC to report annually on its application and petition backlogs.

summary_detail.significance: The bill impacts the commercial space and telecommunications sectors by altering how quickly and predictably companies can obtain federal authorization to operate satellites and ground stations in the United States.
